content.decision_summary: The benzimidazole-piperidine-aryl scaffold is strongly supported as CNS-penetrant by multiple direct rat/PET brain-uptake records, but the query contains a free carboxylic acid plus a basic piperidine, forming a zwitterion that is expected to severely reduce passive BBB permeability. evidence_gaps: No direct brain/plasma, CSF, or uptake data exist for the query molecule or for a close analogue containing the same C(C)(C)C(=O)O carboxylic acid.
Efflux transporter susceptibility (P-gp/BCRP) of the query is unknown and could further reduce CNS access.
Unbound brain concentrations, not just total brain levels, are unavailable for the closest analogues.
